correctness.rationale: A common root of f=x^5+ax+1 and f' is equivalent to a^5=1; the monic trinomial discriminant is 5^5+4^4a^5=4(a^5-1) in characteristic seven. On the smooth locus the tame degree-three cover has six totally ramified points, including one above infinity, giving genus four. At infinity ord(x), ord(y), ord(dx) are -3,-5,-4; the proposed basis orders are 1,6,3,0. At finite branch points dx has order two in parameter y. Rewriting x^i dx/y^j as a seventh-power factor times x^i f^{2j}dx makes the entrywise seventh-power coefficients [x^{7k+6-i}]f^{2j}; an independent polynomial product reproduced both blocks. Expanding the lower block determinant gives a^6+6a, hence the full determinant is 2a^2(a^5-1)=4a^2 times the discriminant. The relative coefficient determinant vanishes exactly to order two at zero on the smooth marked base. At zero the coefficient matrix is F_7-rational and has successive ranks 2,1,0, giving a-number two and stable rank zero; it is invertible at the other smooth parameters. For m=1,2,3 the map x->x^5 permutes F_{7^m}, so there are 7^m+1 exceptional-fiber points. A different field tower (i^2=-1 and j^2=2+i, whose norm down to F_7 is nonsquare 5) gives exactly 2094 points for m=4, and reproduces 2379 for the a=2 cross-check. Replay `python3 /workspace/reproductions/5.py`. Then Newton identities give c_4=-308/4=-77 with c_1=c_2=c_3=0, and the functional equation yields the rest of 1-77T^4+7^4T^8. Valuations give slopes 1/4 and 3/4 each four times. The marked smooth count follows by removing gcd(5,7^m-1) roots of unity. The supplied finite enumerator was inspected, not run; the classification for arbitrary geometric parameters rests on the Cartier identity, not sampling. The zeta polynomial concerns this particular F_7 model only.
